headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 8 studies yielded an effect size of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.7–1.04), indicating no statistically significant association between alcohol and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 86.92%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
